description: We’re ε″, a student team from Uzbekistan tackling soil salinization: salt ruins farmland before it’s visible. We’ll build an interactive web app that maps surface changes in irrigated fields with NISAR radar data, plus our own physics layer explaining why salt and moisture look alike at L-band. We bring radar physics modeling, Python and ML, data analysis and CubeSat experience. Looking for: web/front-end dev, SAR/GIS data processing, UI/UX design and pitch storytelling.

details:
Salt from Space is an open-source web app designed to help identify farmland that may be at risk of soil salinity. We processed six NISAR radar scenes and six soil-moisture maps from June to October 2026—about 15 GB of data—using Python. The app turns the results into interactive maps with a time slider, a before-and-after comparison, point inspection and a guided tour. It is available in English, Russian and Uzbek.

We developed two complementary methods. Global mode uses widely available radar data to flag areas that stay wet but bare throughout the season. In our Mirzachul, Uzbekistan case study, 35% of the mapped area fell into our highest risk class, compared with 13% across the full scene. Precision mode studies the phase difference between horizontal and vertical radar signals. Our physics model predicted a 4–9 degree difference for a salt crust relative to sand. In a comparison between the Rann of Kutch salt flat and nearby desert sand, we observed a 5–14 degree difference across three dates.

Our creative approach combines broad-area screening with a more detailed test based on radar phase. We also considered soil moisture and surface roughness, which can affect radar measurements. The map shows risk indicators, not confirmed salt levels: field samples are still needed to validate the results. Our goal is to help farmers, researchers and land managers decide where to check soil first and where interventions may be needed.
